summary: You were in the hospital because germs infected one of your heart valves. Your heart got weak and fluid built up in your lungs. You need more weeks of antibiotic through your IV line at home. You are also going home with a water pill and a new heart medicine. Get every IV dose, take care of your PICC line, and weigh yourself every day.

diagnoses.plain: Infection of the mitral valve in your heart
Weak heart that does not pump well, with extra fluid (heart failure)
diagnoses.clinical: Acute on chronic heart failure with reduced EF

diagnoses.plain: Fluid in the lungs, now gone
Low red blood cells from long-term illness
Past IV drug use, in recovery
diagnoses.clinical: History of intravenous drug use, in remission

new.name: Cefazolin
new.howOften: through your IV line, at the dose and schedule the infectious-disease team gave you
new.why: The antibiotic that kills the valve infection. Every dose matters. Do not stop or change it on your own.

new.name: Furosemide
new.why: A water pill that keeps fluid from building up. You will urinate more.

new.name: Losartan
new.why: Helps your heart, started at a low dose because your blood pressure and kidneys are still recovering.

continue.name: Metoprolol succinate
continue.howOften: at the dose on your discharge list

continue.name: Other chronic medications
continue.howOften: as on your final medication list

stop.name: Empiric inpatient antibiotics
stop.why: Stopped. The hospital antibiotics were replaced by cefazolin, which targets your exact infection.

stop.name: NSAIDs
stop.why: Avoid pain relievers like ibuprofen unless your doctor says it is okay. They can hurt your heart and kidneys.

checklist.text: Get every IV Cefazolin dose on the schedule from the infectious-disease team
checklist.due: every scheduled dose until the course is complete

checklist.text: Take Furosemide 40 mg once a day
Take Losartan 25 mg once a day
Weigh yourself every day and watch for swelling or breathlessness
Check your PICC line site every day for redness, drainage or bleeding
Get the blood tests on your outpatient antibiotic plan
Go to all cardiology (heart doctor) appointments
Keep your PICC line care appointments
Eat a low-salt diet and follow your fluid plan
Follow any activity limits and dental-procedure advice from your teams

call911: New weakness, a drooping face, trouble speaking, or confusion (signs of stroke)
Sudden severe back, chest or belly pain
goToER: Fever, chills, or feeling very sick again
New or worsening shortness of breath
Swelling or weight going up quickly
Bleeding, a lot of drainage, or redness around the PICC line
callClinic: Any problem with the IV line, such as it will not flush or looks damaged
Questions about your medicines after discharge

followUps.why: Track the antibiotic course and blood tests
Check your heart valve and heart failure plan

followUps.who: Outpatient infusion and PICC care team
followUps.why: Give the IV antibiotic and care for the line

questionsToAsk: Who do I call if my PICC line stops working, day or night?
What should I do if an antibiotic dose is late or missed?
How much weight gain should make me call you?
When will you decide whether I need valve surgery?
Do I need antibiotics before dental work?
